case_name: S. P. Bhatnagar and another v State Of Maharashtra
respondent:
State Of Maharashtra
Supreme Court of India

4 January 1979
Criminal Appeal Nos. 346 and 387 of 1975.
The Judgment was delivered by : Jaswant Singh, J.
1. The above noted two criminal appeals which are directed against the common judgment and order dated August 6, 1975 of the High Court of Judicature at Bombay affirming on appeal the judgment and order dated August 6, 1973 of the Special Judge, Greater Bombay, convicting S. P. Bhatnagar, appellant in the aforesaid first appeal, (hereinafter described as A-1) under s. 120B read with sections 409 and 109 of the Indian Penal Code and s. 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947, and sentencing him to six months simple imprisonment on each of the said two courts as well as convicting A. S. Krishnaswamy, appellant in the aforesaid second appeal (hereinafter described as A-2) under the aforesaid two counts but reducing his sentence from nine months' imprisonment to six months simple imprisonment on each one
facts: The Indian Oil Corporation decided to purchase 13 acres of land from Tata Power House at Trombay.
A survey was conducted to find out the extent of rock cutting and filling required for levelling the area.
Eleven firms submitted tenders, but A-4 abstained. Ram & Co.'s tender was the lowest.
The Engineering Department prepared a comparative statement showing that A-4's tender was the lowest.
A-2 drew up tender committee proceedings recommending that the contract be awarded to A-4 at their quoted rate of Rs. 6,07,807/-
Srivastava refused to accept the recommendations and suggested re-submitting quotations from all contractors.
A-2 carried on with fresh negotiations with A-4 without associating any member of the Finance Department and persuaded him to accept the lowest revised rates offered by Ram & Co.
issues: Whether the tender committee's recommendation was valid
Whether the contract should be awarded to A-4 at their quoted rate
petitioner_arguments: The tender committee's recommendation was valid and the contract should be awarded to A-4 at their quoted rate
respondent_arguments: The tender committee's recommendation was not valid and the contract should not be awarded to A-4 at their quoted rate
holding: The mere initialling by A-1 of the bill alongside the note marked for him by A-2 is not a circumstance which can unmistakably be said to point to the guilt of the appellant.
A-1 and A-2 did not act with any dishonest or corrupt motive or abuse their position.
The appeals are allowed, the convictions are set aside, and the appellants are acquitted of the offences with which they were charged.
